questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How efficient the human body is
Why cheetahs are faster than any car on the road
How Kenyan runners prepare for the Olympic Games
Why salmon swim upriver every year to lay eggs
questions.why: Sam says they'll be asking how efficient the human body is, comparing humans with each other and with animals.

questions.q: Why does Sam mention Olympic swimmers and sprinters?
options: To show that humans are faster than cheetahs
To say that athletes eat much more than other people
To show that human bodies are amazing too
To explain why most people struggle to run
questions.why: After Roy lists amazing animals, Sam says human bodies are 'no less incredible'.

questions.q: According to Roy, why does the human body need to be efficient?
options: Because we have to run away from dangerous animals
It only has the energy that comes from our food
Because humans sleep less than most other animals
Because we need to carry heavy things every day
questions.why: Roy says our bodies work using just the energy from what we eat, so they must use as little as possible.

questions.q: What does Professor Herman Pontzer say makes humans efficient?
options: Our big brains and our ability to plan ahead
Our flat backs and our strong, bent legs
Our small size compared with other apes
Our straight legs, long for our size
questions.why: He says humans have very straight legs that are pretty long for our body size, so we are efficient.

questions.q: How do most animals, such as dogs, stand and move?
options: Bent at the knee and leaning forward
Upright on two long, straight legs
Mostly on their back legs, like apes
With straight legs and a curved back
questions.why: Pontzer says the dog has a bent leg shape and that crouched posture is typical of most animals.

questions.q: According to Rhona Pearce, what is the main reason some athletes run so well?
options: The food they eat as children
Their very long legs and light bones
Training
Living high up in the mountains
questions.why: Roy says the main reason, according to Rhona Pearce, is training, though there are other factors too.

questions.q: What does Rhona say about age and running?
options: Older runners always have better running economy
Age makes no difference if you train hard enough
Children are the most efficient runners of all
Tendons get less stretchy as you get older
questions.why: She says tendon elasticity 'drops off as you get older', so there is a best age for running.

questions.q: What does Rhona say about a runner's weight?
options: Lighter runners are always the fastest ones
More muscle helps; fat must be carried
Weight doesn't matter at all for long distances
Heavier runners use less energy per kilo
questions.why: She says more muscle mass will help you, whereas with more fat 'you've got to carry it'.
